label: TP
reason: Alert 1 (java/xss) is TP because the resolved sink value at L91-L92 is attacker-controlled. The 'sql' string constructed at L67 is derived from 'bar', which is set to valuesList.get(1) where valuesList[1] = param (user input after URL decoding). Although encodeForHTML is called on the final output, the XSS vulnerability stems from the SQL injection path where user input flows directly into the SQL query construction. Alert 2 (java/sql-injection) is also TP because the resolved sink value 'sql' at L67 includes user input directly concatenated into the SQL string.

evidence.note: User input retrieved via getHeader and URL decoded
User input added to list, then first element removed, leaving user input at index 1
SQL query constructed with user input directly concatenated
XSS sink where user input flows into HTML output via SQL query
